extraction.name: WikiText
extraction.description: WikiText is a language modeling benchmark dataset constructed from Wikipedia articles. It is available in two sizes, WikiText-2 and WikiText-103, and preserves punctuation, original casing, numbers, and a larger vocabulary to better support modeling rare words and long-term dependencies.
extraction.creator: Stephen Merity; Caiming Xiong; James Bradbury; Richard Socher
extraction.citeAs: Stephen Merity, Caiming Xiong, James Bradbury, Richard Socher. Pointer Sentinel Mixture Models. arXiv:1609.07843, 2016.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The authors constructed the WikiText dataset by selecting Wikipedia articles that met the Good or Featured article criteria specified by Wikipedia editors, then extracting the text for each article using the Wikipedia API.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web API; Document analysis; Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Text from Wikipedia articles selected from 23,805 Good articles and 4,790 Featured articles, extracted from Wikipedia mark-up using the Wikipedia API.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The Penn Treebank is unrealistic for real language use because tokens are lower case, stripped of punctuation, and limited to a 10k-word vocabulary; other larger-scale language modeling datasets either have restrictive licensing or randomized sentence ordering, which is unrealistic for most language use and prevents effective learning and evaluation of longer-term dependencies
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The authors state that accurately predicting rare words, such as named entities, is an important task for many applications
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset includes named entities such as people’s names and company names from Wikipedia articles.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: language modeling; evaluating how well language models can exploit longer contexts and deal with more realistic vocabularies and larger corpora; improving handling of rare words and the usage of long term dependencies in language modeling
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For the Penn Treebank, words were lower-cased, numbers were replaced with N, newlines were replaced with <eos>, and all other punctuation was removed; the vocabulary was limited to the most frequent 10k words with the rest of the tokens replaced by an <unk> token. For WikiText, text was extracted from Wikipedia articles, sections primarily featuring lists were removed by default, sort keys and Edit buttons that leaked in from the HTML were removed, mathematical formulae and LaTeX code were replaced with <formula> tokens, normalization and tokenization were performed using the Moses tokenizer, slightly augmented to further split numbers, a vocabulary was constructed by discarding all words with a count below 3, and words outside of the vocabulary were mapped to the <unk> token.
